### compose-args: -f compose.yaml
### file: .env
# Generated by `songstress install` — secrets live HERE and only here
# (mode 0600). songstress.lock.json carries no secrets.

# ── basics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
TZ=UTC
PUID=1000
PGID=1000
MUSIC_DIR=/srv/music
SONGSTRESS_PORT=8090
ENABLE_TELEMETRY=true

# ── app admin (sign-in for web, desktop & mobile) ────────────────────────────
SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_EMAIL=a@b.c
SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=sct.admin.7f3k

# ── public URL (set this if you front Songstress with a proxy/tunnel) ────────
# The origin you serve Songstress on, e.g. https://music.example.com. Makes
# invite & password-reset email links resolve; blank is fine on a LAN.
SONGSTRESS_PUBLIC_URL=

# ── Navidrome (managed sibling service) ──────────────────────────────────────
NAVIDROME_PORT=4533
NAVIDROME_PASSWORD=sct.nd.7f3k

### file: compose.yaml
# Generated by `songstress install` — regenerate with `songstress reconfigure`.
# Songstress (datastore, dashboard, acquisition worker) + official Navidrome.

# Container log rotation: Docker's default json-file driver never rotates, so
# the logs would grow until the disk fills. 10 x 50 MB per service keeps well
# over the 14 days an incident review needs.
x-logging: &logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: "50m"
    max-file: "10"

services:
  songstress:
    image: ghcr.io/pacholoamit/songstress:v0.33.0
    container_name: songstress
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - PUID=${PUID}
      - PGID=${PGID}
      - SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_EMAIL=${SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_EMAIL}
      - SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${SONGSTRESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD}
      # Public URL — the origin your reverse proxy / tunnel serves this on. Sets
      # the app URL baked into invite & password-reset email links (otherwise
      # they point at http://localhost:8090). Empty is fine on a LAN.
      - SONGSTRESS_PUBLIC_URL=${SONGSTRESS_PUBLIC_URL:-}
      - ENABLE_TELEMETRY=${ENABLE_TELEMETRY}
      # The release this server runs, as the apps see it: they compare it with
      # their own version and say when one side needs updating.
      - APP_VERSION=0.33.0
      - MUSIC_LIBRARIES=Main=/music
      # Managed Navidrome: Songstress provisions and drives the service below,
      # and serves every stream and cover itself.
      - SONGSTRESS_MANAGED_NAVIDROME=1
      - NAVIDROME_URL=http://navidrome:4533
      - NAVIDROME_USERNAME=admin
      - NAVIDROME_PASSWORD=${NAVIDROME_PASSWORD}
      # Email (optional; empty host/to = disabled). Set via `.env` — the install
      # wizard's SMTP group writes them; these defaults cover the unset case.
      - SMTP_HOST=${SMTP_HOST:-}
      - SMTP_PORT=${SMTP_PORT:-587}
      - SMTP_USERNAME=${SMTP_USERNAME:-}
      - SMTP_PASSWORD=${SMTP_PASSWORD:-}
      - SMTP_FROM=${SMTP_FROM:-}
      - SMTP_TO=${SMTP_TO:-}
      - SMTP_STARTTLS=${SMTP_STARTTLS:-true}
    ports:
      # Published on the host — front this with your own reverse proxy, tunnel,
      # or tailnet. Songstress terminates no TLS of its own.
      - "${SONGSTRESS_PORT}:8090"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/pb/pb_data
      - ${MUSIC_DIR}:/music
    # Bounded scratch space: provider credential caches, in-flight Soulseek
    # transfers and one Wrapped render fit in 1.5 GiB; past it a write fails
    # and is retried instead of the container running out of memory.
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:mode=1777,size=${SONGSTRESS_TMP_SIZE:-1536m}
    depends_on:
      navidrome:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    # Ceilings so one runaway process (a wedged render, an ffmpeg pile-up) can't
    # starve the host. CPU caps are off (0); set one only to a count your host has.
    mem_limit: ${SONGSTRESS_MEM_LIMIT:-4g}
    cpus: ${SONGSTRESS_CPUS:-0}

  navidrome:
    image: deluan/navidrome:0.62.0
    container_name: songstress-navidrome
    user: "${PUID}:${PGID}"
    depends_on:
      navidrome-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - ND_MUSICFOLDER=/music
      - ND_DATAFOLDER=/data
      - ND_PORT=4533
      # Songstress triggers scans after acquisitions — no double-scanning.
      - ND_SCANNER_SCHEDULE=0
      - ND_SCANNER_WATCHERWAIT=0
      - ND_SCANNER_SCANONSTARTUP=true
      - ND_ENABLETRANSCODINGCONFIG=true
      # Creates the 'admin' user on Navidrome's FIRST boot only.
      - ND_DEVAUTOCREATEADMINPASSWORD=${NAVIDROME_PASSWORD}
    ports:
      # Optional: Navidrome's own web UI for admin and debugging. The apps never
      # need it — Songstress serves all media itself. Safe to drop.
      - "${NAVIDROME_PORT}:4533"
    volumes:
      # ND data nested under the datastore root — one directory to back up.
      - ./data/navidrome:/data
      - ${MUSIC_DIR}:/music:ro
    healthcheck:
      # The official image ships no HEALTHCHECK; songstress gates on this.
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://127.0.0.1:4533/ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    logging: *logging
    # Sized for a full scan, not for idling: a cap below the scan's peak would
    # kill it mid-scan, and the scan-on-start above would loop.
    mem_limit: ${NAVIDROME_MEM_LIMIT:-3g}
    cpus: ${NAVIDROME_CPUS:-0}

  # One-shot: hands ./data/navidrome to PUID:PGID before Navidrome starts. On
  # Linux, Docker creates a missing bind-mount source as root; Navidrome (running
  # as PUID:PGID) then can't write its database, never turns healthy, and
  # songstress, waiting on that health check, never starts. Same image as
  # Navidrome, so nothing extra is pulled.
  navidrome-init:
    image: deluan/navidrome:0.62.0
    user: "0:0"
    entrypoint: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /data && chown ${PUID}:${PGID} /data"]
    volumes:
      - ./data/navidrome:/data
    restart: "no"
    logging: *logging
